summary: Iter61 — Platform-wide CTA modal form system. Backend: 19/19 pytest cases pass on /app/backend/tests/test_iter61_cta_forms.py covering (a) auto-provisioning across 7 templates (real_estate, education, healthcare, legal, hospitality, construction, saas), (b) EXACT industry-aware field-spec verification (name/type/required + option lists) for 6 industries against the spec in Part 2, plus fallback for saas, (c) public /public/site/{token}/cta-forms + submit — including 400 on missing-required and 200 on full submit — with a lead landing in the tenant's /apps/{id}/inbox tagged with form_label, (d) email-field protection (PUT that omits email → 400) and unsupported field type → 400, (e) per-tenant isolation (edit A → B unchanged), (f) rescan detecting a new qualifying label 'Request a callback' with FALLBACK fields and NOT provisioning a non-qualifying 'Our story', (g) client editor simplified=true, can_edit=true with 403/404 for other tenants. Frontend: verified on tenant app_d8a1146c7426 (healthcare, preview pv_e72ca0b15cbe1463cd72e2fa) that (1) cta-btn-book-an-appointment renders, (2) cta-modal opens over a dark backdrop rgba(0,0,0,0.7) with X, backdrop-click, and Escape all closing it, (3) form fields have the healthcare industry spec, (4) full submit shows cta-modal-success containing 'We\'ll be in touch within 24 hours.', (5) admin AppDetail /apps/{id} has a Forms tab with data-testid cta-forms-panel listing every CTA, (6) editor opens with cta-form-title-input, cta-form-success-input, cta-add-field-btn, and email's remove + required buttons are BOTH disabled in the UI as required. ONE CRITICAL VISUAL BUG FOUND (see rca): the modal's submit button loses its brand colour because CtaFormModal portals to document.body which is OUTSIDE the theme-var scope set on <div data-testid=public-preview-page>.

ui_bugs.issue: Submit button computed backgroundColor is rgba(0,0,0,0) — the tenant's primary brand colour (Part 3 requirement) is not applied because `var(--tp)`, `var(--tbg)`, `var(--tbody)`, `var(--tbd)`, `var(--tr)`, `var(--tsf)`, `var(--thead)`, `var(--tmut)`, `var(--tfh)`, `var(--tfb)` are all empty inside the modal. themeVars() sets these on <div data-testid=public-preview-page> in /app/frontend/src/pages/PublicPreview.jsx:68, but CtaFormModal uses createPortal(..., document.body) so its subtree is outside that theme scope and inherits nothing. Verified: same page reports page_tp='#0D9488' but bd_tp='' and modal_bg=rgba(0,0,0,0). The modal still renders because default browser text colours coincidentally read; the submit CTA however is completely invisible until hovered/clicked, breaking the 'submit button in the tenant\'s primary brand colour labelled with the original button intent' spec.

action_items: Fix the theme-var leak on the CTA modal portal. Options: (a) render CtaFormModal as a child of the themed preview <div> instead of portalling to body, (b) apply themeVars(site.theme) to the portal wrapper too (pass theme via CtaCtx and set inline style on the outer div inside CtaFormModal), or (c) hoist tenant theme vars to document.documentElement / :root when PublicPreview mounts and unset on unmount. Same fix must also apply to the builder overlay so the Submit button carries the tenant primary colour there.

Add a defensive fallback for --tp on the submit button style (e.g. `background: var(--tp, ${site.theme.primary})`) — even after the scope fix — so ChatWidget / any future portal never silently loses brand colour.
critical_code_review_comments: CtaFormModal.jsx uses createPortal(..., document.body) which escapes the theme-var scope. This is the root cause of the submit-button/backdrop-colour regression. Passing theme through CtaCtx and applying it via inline style on the outermost portal div (or moving the modal in-tree) is the fix.
Positive: cta_forms.py enforces the email field on the server (PUT rejects fields lacking email with 400), matches the UI's disabled remove/required buttons — client and server contracts agree.

Positive: cta_labels() only walks props.cta / cta2 / submit_label / plan names, and CTA_PATTERN uses word-boundary \b matching, so 'Patient portal', 'Our story', 'About us' correctly do NOT generate forms (verified live).
Public submit path writes both a message (via inbox.new_message with form_label meta) AND a submissions row — good redundancy for the Leads view Source column.
Per-tenant isolation is guaranteed by keying cta_forms on {app_id, key} and never referencing another app in _provision — verified by mutating tenant A and re-reading tenant B unchanged.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% — all functional flows pass; one high-priority visual bug on submit button brand colour

rca of the issue:
CTA modal submit button not showing tenant brand colour. RCA: /app/frontend/src/pages/PublicPreview.jsx:68 applies themeVars(site.theme) — which returns {--tp, --tbg, --tbody, --tbd, --thead, --tmut, --tsf, --tfh, --tfb, --tr, ...} — as inline style on
. CSS custom properties inherit only through the DOM tree. /app/frontend/src/components/CtaFormModal.jsx:65 wraps its markup in createPortal(
...
, document.body). document.body is a sibling of, not a descendant of, public-preview-page — so none of the tenant theme vars are inherited. On the styled DOM this manifests as `getComputedStyle(cta-modal-submit).backgroundColor === 'rgba(0,0,0,0)'` even though `getComputedStyle(public-preview-page).getPropertyValue('--tp') === '#0D9488'`. Fix: either apply themeVars to the portal wrapper (recommended — pass theme through CtaCtx and set style={themeVars(theme)} on the outer div inside CtaFormModal), or set the vars on :root while the modal is open. Both cta_modal (bg), cta_modal (border), field surfaces, labels and the submit button will pick up the correct colours once the vars cascade.
